title: Region safelist replication hierarchy and tenant failover policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a region safelist-based replication hierarchy and tenant failover policy for analytics ingestion and materialized views. Goal: ensure customers with region constraints only have telemetry replicated to allowed regions while enabling deterministic automatic failover for availability. This ticket covers schema and metadata tagging, router changes to respect safelist tiers, replication orchestration changes (source -> local -> permitted mirrors), and a controlled failover path when local region ingestion is degraded.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry messages from tenants with a configured region safelist are only written to Kafka/topic partitions that are routed to permitted regions
Control-plane metadata (tenant.region_safelist and replication_tier) is stored and queryable from the tenancy catalog and respected by the ingestion router
Failover path promotes a single permitted secondary region when primary region SLO is breached and does not replicate outside the tenant safelist
Automated integration test coverage for replication enforcement, failover trigger, and rollback behavior
Rolling deployment plan with canary on 5% of tenants and monitoring dashboards showing replication health and wrong-region writes at zero for safelisted tenants
design_decisions: Use a two-level safelist: explicit regions (e.g., eu-west-1) and logical region groups (e.g., ‘EU’). Tenant entries can include both. This reduces per-tenant config while keeping legal granularity.
Replication will follow a hierarchy: primary-local -> secondary-permitted -> tertiary-permitted (only when explicitly enabled). Default tertiary disabled to limit cross-border risk.
Router will perform a metadata lookup with local cache and TTL=30s to avoid per-request datastore hits; callbacks will invalidate cache on tenant update events.

Failover detection based on ingestion consumer lag + region SLO breach signals from the console (latency > 99p threshold for 2 minutes) with a 3-step guard: detection -> dry-run routing -> commit and notify.
We will not attempt cross-tenant co-mingling to satisfy throughput; replication units remain tenant-scoped to simplify rollbacks and audits.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy router changes and safelist metadata reads to ingestion-candidates cluster. Enable for 5% low-throughput tenants. Duration: 72 hours.
Phase 2 (Validation): Run synthetic ingest tests and compare materialized view parity. Validate zero wrong-region writes for canary tenants. Duration: 72 hours.
Phase 3 (Scoped ramp): Increase to 25% of tenants and enable secondary region failover dry-run (no commit). Monitor metrics and runbook playthroughs. Duration: 5 days.
Phase 4 (Full enable): Enable actual failover commit for safelisted tenants and open rollout; continue monitoring and schedule a rollback window. Duration: gradual over 2 weeks.
Rollback: revert router feature flag and drain canary topics; run full audit for any out-of-safelist writes.
